input.quote: Except to the extent any jointly-owned inventions or intellectual property are included in subject matter licensed by one Party to the other Party under this Agreement, each Party may only practice any such jointly-owned inventions or intellectual property for its own internal purposes, and neither Party shall have the right to enforce, license, or assign such jointly- owned inventions or intellectual property, without the prior written consent of the other Party.
input.rationale: Section 11.1 keeps Ono's solely-created IP with Ono (11.1(a)) and Array's with Array (11.1(b)), so there is no assignment of our IP to Array. However, 11.1(c) creates joint ownership of jointly-made inventions and 11.1(d) strips it of any exploitation right: each Party may practice joint IP only for internal purposes and may not enforce, license or assign it without the other's consent. That is joint ownership without an unrestricted right to exploit - the walk-away outcome under this rule - and it also fails the fallback, which requires us to hold a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free right to use, modify and sublicense the jointly created work product for our business. Deleting joint ownership to reach the preferred position would require collateral rewrites of the Joint Invention/Joint Patent/Joint Know-How definitions, Section 11.2(b) and the Article II licences, so we take the fallback: we leave the joint-ownership structure and the carve-out for subject matter licensed between the Parties intact, and simply free Ono's side of Section 11.1(d) (made subject to Section 2.1(d) so the no-modification covenant on Binimetinib/Encorafenib is preserved), while leaving Array's consent restriction unchanged. Separately, the Section 2.6 Grant-Back License reaches Ono Know-How and Data through the "Improvement" definition and lets Array sublicense it through multiple tiers to make and sell Products, i.e. independent exploitation of our data; we add a short proviso limiting Array's licence in our Data and Ono Know-How to performing its obligations under this Agreement. Section 4.8's rights of reference are mutual and already tied to performance under this Agreement, and Section 14.2(a)(v)'s post-expiry reversion is left untouched as a termination-effects term.

proposal.summary: Give Ono an unrestricted right to exploit jointly-owned IP and limit Array's grant-back licence in Ono Data
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Joint ownership here comes with no right to exploit: neither Party may license or assign joint IP and each may only practice it internally, which is walk-away territory for us. We have kept the joint-ownership structure but taken our playbook fallback - a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free right for Ono to use, modify, license and sublicense the jointly-owned IP for its business - and limited Array's grant-back licence in our Data and Ono Know-How to performing its obligations under this Agreement.

ops.newText: Ono shall have a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free right to practice, use, modify, license and sublicense any such jointly-owned inventions or intellectual property for its business without Array's consent, subject to Section 2.1(d); and Array may only practice such jointly-owned inventions or intellectual property for its own internal purposes and shall not enforce, license, or assign the same without Ono's prior written consent.

ops.text: The Grant-Back License, to the extent it extends to any Data or Ono Know-How, is limited to Array's use of such Data and Ono Know-How solely to perform its obligations under this Agreement.
